title: Neural Networks
overview: A neural network is a system of connected nodes inspired by how the human brain works.

blocks.title: What is What is a Neural Network?
blocks.body: A neural network is a system of connected nodes inspired by how the human brain works.
bullets: Human neurons pass electrical signals; AI nodes pass numbers
Each node takes inputs, multiplies by weights, adds them up, produces output
Layers: Input Layer (receives data) → Hidden Layers (processes) → Output Layer (gives result)
Training adjusts weights over thousands of examples until outputs are correct
This concept is fundamental to AI development.

analogy.title: Think of Neural Networks as a Team of Detectives
analogy.description: Each detective specializes in one clue — an edge, a color, a shape. Together they combine findings to solve the case. Each neuron detects one pattern; layers combine them to recognize complex objects.

code.code:
# Single neuron: weighted sum + activation
inputs = [0.5, 0.8, 0.2]
weights = [0.4, -0.3, 0.6]
output = sum(i * w for i, w in zip(inputs, weights))
print(f"Neuron output: {output:.2f}")
print("Activated!" if output > 0 else "Not activated")

blocks.question: Does a neural network learn by adjusting its weights during training?
blocks.answer: Yes, adjusting weights reduces the error and trains the model.

blocks.title: What is Deep Learning & CNNs?
blocks.body: Deep Learning uses neural networks with many hidden layers. CNNs are specialized for images.
bullets: Deep Learning = neural networks with many hidden layers
More layers = ability to learn more complex patterns
CNNs (Convolutional Neural Networks) — specialized for recognizing patterns in images
Real-world uses: face unlock on phones, voice recognition (Alexa, Siri), medical image diagnosis
Why neural networks need lots of data — more examples = better and more reliable learning

analogy.title: Think of CNN as a Magnifying Glass Scanning a Photo
analogy.description: A magnifying glass slides across a photo, examining small patches at a time. Each patch reveals local patterns: edges → textures → objects. CNNs convolve filters across images to detect visual features.

code.code:
# CNN-style: sliding window convolution
image = [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0]
filter = [1, -1]
output = []
for i in range(len(image) - 1):
    output.append(image[i] * filter[0] + image[i+1] * filter[1])
print(f"Convolved: {output}")

blocks.question: Do self-driving cars use neural networks to recognize what they see on the road?
blocks.answer: Yes, they use advanced CNNs to process camera feeds and detect objects.

blocks.title: What is NN Steps?
bullets: Step 1: Define input — what data goes into the network (numbers, image pixels, text)
Step 2: Set up layers — input layer, hidden layers, output layer
Step 3: Initialize weights — start with random numbers
Step 4: Train — feed examples, compare output to correct answer, adjust weights
Step 5: Test — give new unseen data, measure accuracy

analogy.title: Think of Neural Network Layers as a Factory Assembly Line
analogy.description: Raw materials enter. Each station transforms the product. Early stations handle simple tasks, later ones build complex assemblies. Information flows forward through network layers, each building on the last.

code.code:
# Forward pass through layers
def layer(inputs, weights, bias):
    return [max(0, sum(i*w for i,w in zip(inputs, w_row)) + b) for w_row, b in zip(weights, bias)]

x = [1, 0, 1]
w1 = [[0.5, -0.2, 0.1], [-0.3, 0.8, -0.1]]
b1 = [0, 0]
h1 = layer(x, w1, b1)
print(f"After layer 1: {h1}")

blocks.answer: Not always! It depends on the specific problem and constraints.

keyTakeaways.text: Neural networks are inspired by how the human brain processes information
Each node takes inputs, multiplies by weights, and produces an output
Training adjusts weights until the network makes correct predictions
Deep Learning uses many hidden layers for complex tasks
CNNs specialize in image recognition — used in face unlock, medical scans
